title: Engineering 'Golden' Fluorescence by Selective Pressure Incorporation of Non-canonical Amino Acids and Protein Analysis by Mass Spectrometry and Fluorescence
protocol: Transform chemically or electrocompetent cells of a Trp-auxotrophic E. coli strain with 1 μL of a 1 ng/μL aqueous solution of the pQE-80L His6-ECFP plasmid.
Incubate transformed cells on LB-agar plates supplemented with 10 g/L glucose and 100 µg/mL ampicillin at 37 °C overnight.
Prepare 5 mL of LB medium supplemented with 10 g/L glucose and 100 μg/mL ampicillin in a sterile 14 mL polystyrene culture tube.
Inoculate the prepared LB medium with a single colony from an agar plate using a sterile pipette tip or inoculation loop.
Incubate the cells at 37 °C in an orbital shaker at 200-250 rpm overnight.
Inoculate 10 mL fresh LB medium supplemented with 10 g/L glucose and 100 μg/mL ampicillin with 100 µL of the overnight culture in a 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate the flask at 37 °C in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm.
Inoculate 10 mL of NMM19 medium supplemented with 100 µg/mL ampicillin, 15 µM tryptophan and 10 µL of overnight culture in a 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Incubate the culture overnight at 30 °C in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm.
Measure OD600 every 30 min until the value only changes by less than 0.05 over 30 min.
Take sample "before induction" for SDS-PAGE when the OD600 reaches 0.5-0.8.
Adjust liquid culture to 0.5 mM IPTG and incubate at 30 °C in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm for 4-8 h.
Take sample "after expression" for SDS-PAGE.
Harvest bacterial cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 5,000 x g and 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Freeze cell pellets at -20 °C or -80 °C until target protein purification.
Harvest bacterial cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 5,000 x g and 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Resuspend the cells in 10 mL of NMM19 medium with 100 μg/mL ampicillin into a 100 mL Erlenmeyer flask.
Add 4-amino-indole to a final concentration of 1 mM using 50 mM stock solution.
Incubate for 30 min at 30 °C in an orbital shaker at 200 rpm.
Harvest the bacterial cells by centrifugation for 10 min at 5,000 x g and 4 °C.
Discard the supernatant by decanting.
Take sample "after expression" for SDS-PAGE.
Measure OD600 of the bacterial culture.
Transfer the cell pellet into a 50 mL conical polystyrene tube using a spatula if necessary.
Freeze the cell pellet at -20 °C or -80 °C until target protein purification.
Thaw the cell pellet on ice for 10-20 min.
Resuspend the cell pellet in a 50 mL conical polystyrene tube using 5 mL of ice-cold binding buffer on ice.
Add 20 µL of 50 mg/mL lysozyme, 20 µL of 1 mg/mL DNase I, and 20 µL of 1 mg/mL RNase A.
Close the tube, mix gently by inverting 5 times, and keep it on ice for 30 min.
Lyse the cells by sonication using an ultrasound homogenizer tip with three cycles of 3 min in a 15 mL polystyrene tube cooled by slush ice, with 2 s of pulse, 4 s of pause, and 45% amplitude.
Centrifuge the sample for 30 min at 15,000-18,000 x g, 4 °C.
Transfer the supernatant into a fresh tube and note down the liquid volume.
Filter the solution through a 0.45 µm syringe filter using a 5 mL plastic Luer lock syringe and a polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) syringe filter.
Take sample "lysate" for SDS-PAGE.
Resuspend cell debris pellet in ddH2O (equal volume as former lysate).
Take sample "pellet" for SDS-PAGE.
Use a 1 mL prepacked or self-packed IMAC FPLC column according to manufacturer’s instructions.
Equilibrate the column with binding buffer (Table 1).
Wash the column with binding buffer following application of cell lysate.
Collect and pool eluate fractions that appear as golden color due to GdFP.
Optionally, elute target protein using a linear imidazole gradient (0-250 mM) with an automated FPLC system.
Determine protein concentration using the extinction coefficient at 466 nm (ɛ466 nm = 23,700 M-1 cm-1).
Take sample "eluate" for SDS-PAGE analysis.
Use 1-10 µg of protein per lane depending on staining method and dye sensitivity.
Dialyze an aliquot of eluate fractions against dialysis buffer or MS buffer using a membrane with a MWCO of 5,000-10,000.
Prepare dialysis membrane according to manufacturer's instructions.
Dialyze a 1 mL sample three times against 100 mL buffer for at least 2 h.
Freeze protein sample in dialysis buffer at -80 °C for storage.
Transfer a cell suspension equivalent to 1 mL of OD600 = 1 into a 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tube.
Centrifuge the cells for 10 min at 5000 x g, room temperature.
Discard the supernatant by pipetting.
Add 80 μL of ddH2O and 20 μL of 5x SDS loading dye buffer to the cell pellet.
Mix by pipetting.
Heat the samples to 95 °C for 5 min in a water bath or heat block.
Cool the samples to room temperature.
Use 10 µL for Coomassie-stained SDS-PAGE according to previous publication35.
Determine the protein concentration from a sample dialyzed against MS buffer using MS buffer as reference.
Dilute the protein sample to 0.1 mg/mL using MS buffer for a final volume of 80 μL.
Mix by careful pipetting.
Transfer the solution into an MS autosampler vial with glass insert and close it with a cap.
Remove air bubbles by flicking the vial.
Fill a second autosampler vial without glass insert with 1 mL of MS buffer.
Allow the instrument to warm up.
Perform instrument calibration.
Ensure sufficient amounts of liquid chromatography-grade solvents are available (>100 mL).
Program a linear 20 min HPLC gradient from 5% to 80% buffer A (0.1 % formic acid in ddH2O), combined with buffer B (0.1 % formic acid in acetonitrile).
Start HPLC at a flow of 0.3 mL/min and wait until the column pressure is stable.
Set an autosampler injection volume of 5 µL for the LC-ESI-TOF-MS method.
Create a worklist for a blank run followed by a sample run and assign the corresponding autosampler vial positions.
Run the worklist.
Open the generated sample data file after worklist completion.
Select a range in the total ion current (TIC) plot for deconvolution.
Deconvolute the MS spectrum using the maximum entropy deconvolution algorithm.
Prepare 2 mL of a 1 µM solution of GdFP by dilution into PBS buffer at pH 7.
Fill the GdFP solution into a 1 cm quartz cuvette.
Install ps-pulsed 470 nm laser for sample excitation and the 488 nm long-pass emission filter.
Adjust 600 L/mm grating of the TWCSPC detector for acquisition of the wavelength regime 500-700 nm.

Acquire fluorescence emission at a count rate of about 200 x 103 photons/s until about 103 counts are accumulated in the acquisition maximum of the fluorescence decay curves with single photon counting software.
Replace the sample cuvette with a 1 cm quartz cuvette filled with 1 g/L colloidal silica (~220 m2/g) in PBS buffer at pH 7.
Remove the 488 nm long-pass emission filter and insert grey filters to adjust the count rate at the TWCSPC detector to below 100 x 103 counts/s.
Adjust grating for the acquisition of 470 nm photons in channel 8 of the 16-channel TWCSPC detector.
Acquire the IRF until about 10 x 103 counts are accumulated in the emission maximum.
Convert fluorescence decay curves and IRF to ASCII data files with global fitting program.
Conduct a global fit according to a model of a sum of three exponential components with lifetimes as linked parameters.
Plot decay associated spectra (DAS) as amplitude distributions of individual decay components in dependency of the wavelength with data analysis software.
